note: 4.3-N2 A3 rules 4.3.7 and 4.3.8 applied unchanged to the 116-column pool
statement: Note N1 said a redundancy rule for the 116-column pool needed a dated rule before it was run. This is that rule, fixed before the run. Nothing about the pool has been computed when this is written.

rule.pool: the 80 raw columns plus the 36 adjusted columns (<name>__sadj), 116 in all; overnight_return_open in neither set.
rule.4.3.7: A3 unchanged, applied to each of the 116 columns by its own coverage (finite TRAIN rows over all TRAIN grid rows, percent rounded to 3 decimals, as in Step 6). Primary = at least 80% in both eras. Sensitivity = all 116 on RAW. The result is compared with N1's statement that an adjusted column inherits its raw column's eligibility, and any difference is reported.
rule.4.3.8: A3 unchanged: Spearman on TRAIN rows, pairwise-complete and re-ranked per pair, per era; redundant if |rho| > 0.95 in either era (primary set) or in RAW (sensitivity set); columns are processed in priority order and kept unless redundant with a column already kept.
rule.priority: (1) shorter window = the raw column's Step 4 lookback in bars (an adjusted column has its raw column's window); (2) higher coverage = the lower of the two eras' coverage in the primary set and the RAW coverage in the sensitivity set, each column by its own coverage; (3) position.
rule.position_of_adjusted_columns: Decided by the repository owner in the working session on this date: raw wins ties. Raw columns keep their A3 dictionary positions 0-79; the adjusted columns take positions 80-115 in the order of A3's scale-feature list. This is the only element not already in A3.

outputs_promised: primary and RAW-sensitivity counts (pool size, kept, dropped, split raw/adjusted), hashed, added to the closing report as an addendum without editing the closed report.
